commits.summary: Follow ordinary Spring startup through JDK calls (verification pending)
commits.body:
Run application cache initializers and the selected JDK's lock, reference queue, writer, collection and iterator bytecode. The native checker follows concrete zero-limit splits, directly declared method and field metadata, and fresh same-thread bindings. Overriding initial values, unresolved member signatures and unbound VM configuration retain their proof boundaries.

The real fixed Spring Security manager passed a capped strict proof of four decisions: an indirect grant, its loss after removing the B-to-D edge, a preserved direct grant and a C-only denial. The original JVM confirmed all four. Pinned Temurin 21 tool tests cover aliases, overrides, lookup misses, writer identity and both possible immutable-set orders. The four example validators, eight frozen tables, existing scorecards, 59 selected Rust binaries and all selected Python suites passed. The negative HashSet capacity in the conformance corpus now refutes on the original JDK bytecode.

Job 20261123-011836-recheck-all-ordinary-spring-claims-after checks the 16 Spring primary claims and two binder controls on the original classpaths. Job 20261123-012155-check-spring-startup-changes-against-the checks the proof-tier conformance corpus under JBMC, auto and confirmation.

commits.summary: Record four ordinary Spring role proofs and the startup gaps
commits.body:
Both original legacy hierarchies established the exact reachable authority names and public manager decisions for both prefixes and all 16 authority subsets. The four claims account for 128 complete strict selector proofs and move Spring to 4/16 ordinary native decisions. Four additional proofs on the independently identified historical JARs reproduced the loss of the indirect grant after the B-to-D edge was removed while preserving direct-D grants and C-only denials.

Keep the original attempts, finite observations, new raw refusals and the selector where each public claim stopped. The remaining primary steps are the factory cache key hash, PrintWriter bootstrap registration, ClassUtils' capacity-nine identity map and the UTC TimeZone lookup. The separate 6.1.7 binder control still stops at its cache initializer. The data scorecard reproduced byte for byte.

All 130 managed output hashes matched, 15 damaged selector records and 10 damaged or misattributed edge-control records were rejected, all eight oracle tables reproduced and the four example validators passed. All 59 selected Rust binaries and all 27 selected Python suites passed. The independent proof-tier conformance job 20261123-012155-check-spring-startup-changes-against-the is still running.
